kf: **Primary adrenal insufficiency**: failure of the adrenal cortex, with low cortisol and aldosterone. About 100–140 per million in the UK.
70–90% is **autoimmune** in the UK; other causes include TB, metastases, haemorrhage and drugs.
Skin clue: **hyperpigmentation** of creases, scars, gums, knuckles and pressure areas; vitiligo may coexist.
**Adrenal crisis** (vomiting, hypotension, collapse) → 999 and **hydrocortisone 100 mg IM/IV immediately** (NICE NG243).
Every patient needs an **NHS Steroid Emergency Card**, injection kit and **sick-day rules**.
myths: **"Pigmentation happens in all adrenal insufficiency"**: only primary (high ACTH); secondary causes are pale.
patho_lead: Pigmentation comes from **excess ACTH**, which also stimulates melanocytes.

mech.t: Low cortisol removes negative feedback, so the pituitary makes more POMC.
POMC is cut into ACTH and α-MSH.
ACTH and α-MSH stimulate MC1R on melanocytes, increasing melanin, most visibly in creases and mucosa.
mech.cap: Excess ACTH and MSH from the pituitary drive melanocytes to make more pigment.

comp: Adrenal crisis (fatal if untreated), hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia, hypoglycaemia.
prog: Normal life expectancy with replacement and crisis prevention.
